paras: The killing of a Black prisoner near Horn Lake, Mississippi, took place in late August 1881, when four or five armed men stopped a marshal taking an unnamed Black man to jail at Hernando, ordered the marshal away and shot the prisoner dead on the road. The Memphis Daily Appeal reported it as a murder, and no arrests were reported.

According to the Appeal, the man, "whose name is not known," had a "difficulty" with a farmer named Henry Douglas "about some matter." The outcome of that dispute was that he was tried and committed to jail by a magistrate, though the report names no offense.

The marshal "of the place" set out with the prisoner for the jail at Hernando and had gone only a mile or two, to a point near "the old Fletcher place" on the Hernando plank road, when four or five men armed with guns met them. The men "commanded him to leave his man" and, in the paper's words, "persuaded the Marshal that it was to his interest to leave." Once the marshal had gone, they fired "a broadside" into the prisoner, "literally riddling him and killing him on the spot."

The killing had been "kept suppressed" until the day before the Appeal's report. When the report was written, the attackers had not been arrested and the marshal "had taken no steps looking that way," and no report of an inquest or trial was found.

The Memphis Daily Appeal carried the only original account on August 26 under the headline "RIODLED WITH BALLS. A Negro Murdered at Hernando by a Party of Five," which placed the killing at Hernando and fixed the party at five, while its text said Horn Lake and "four or five." The Appeal called the attackers "the murderers" but referred to the victim as "the darky" and offered no comment on the marshal's withdrawal.
Two weeks later, on September 8, the Weekly Clarion of Jackson reprinted the story without attribution in its "ALL OVER THE STATE" column, adding that Horn Lake was in DeSoto county.

reader.title: Killing of a Black prisoner near Horn Lake, Mississippi
bases: Four or five armed men stopped a marshal taking a committed Black prisoner to jail, made the marshal leave, and shot the prisoner dead on the road [A1].

An armed party of four or five men took a prisoner from a marshal and killed him, which the Appeal called a 'murder' [A1]; the papers state no motive, though the victim had just been committed to jail over a 'difficulty' with a white farmer, so a pretext of punishing him is implied rather than stated [A1].
The Memphis Daily Appeal is the only original report [A1]; the Weekly Clarion item is a condensed reprint of it [A6], and no follow-up, inquest or arrest report was found.

accounts.label: Memphis Daily Appeal report
accounts.gist: An unsourced local report that four or five armed men met the marshal and his prisoner on the Hernando plank road, persuaded the marshal to leave, and riddled the prisoner with shot; the affair had been kept quiet and no one had been arrested.

framing.detail: The Appeal headlined the killing 'A Negro Murdered' and called the men 'the murderers,' while referring to the victim as 'the darky' and printing no comment on the marshal's withdrawal.
The Weekly Clarion of Jackson reprinted the story without attribution or comment in its state news column two weeks later.

versions.value: Horn Lake, a mile or two out on the Hernando plank road (text)

conflicts.note: The headline and the body of the same article differ; the body is more specific and is followed here.
Both versions are in the one report.

record_check.dossier: Killing only: the men ordered the marshal away and shot the prisoner where they met him; he was not carried off.
Supported in the sense that he was in the marshal's custody on the road to jail when the armed men made the marshal leave; not a jail seizure.
The killing took place a mile or two from Horn Lake on the Hernando plank road near the old Fletcher place; the headline says 'at Hernando'.

record_check.dossier: One original report plus a reprint in the Weekly Clarion of September 8.

info: Late August 1881, 'a few days' before the August 26 report; the matter was 'kept suppressed until yesterday'
On the Hernando plank road near 'the old Fletcher place,' about a mile or two from Horn Lake on the way to the jail at Hernando; the Appeal's headline places it 'at Hernando'
One Black man, 'whose name is not known'
